detail.longDescription: Like most, I was stoked on LLMs when they became available. Particularly on the earlier free tiers where the slightly questionable answers were offset by generous tokens. Now, I'm finding that having to use this tech is becoming much less fun. The constant corrections, the constant prompting for greater brevity, the grating certainty and sycophancy. Others probably are forgiving considering the net benefit. But for me it honestly now feels like a chore, which is reflected in how my frustration is now appearing in how I communicate to it now. Instead of articulating and making my prompts precise, I'm just straight-out blurting. Typos, missed words, poor semantic structure - I guess I maybe at some point reasoned that "it will get the picture, so why waste effort being articulate?" Or maybe I'm just anticipating that it is going to get it 15 percent wrong, so why even try and be articulate. Just blurt and steer. Blurt and steer. Is anyone else finding this? I actually sometimes worry about it. I feel it's not just the fact that I'm offloading my cognition to it that is making me dumber, it is the way I'm communicating with it. They say the act of writing is tied to the act of thinking, and my prompts are basicslly the typographic equivalent of grunting right now.
